 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Following his trade to the Dallas Cowboys in 2025, wide receiver George Pickens looked like he was a true No. 1 WR. That was even despite sharing targets with one of the NFL's top wideouts in CeeDee Lamb.
 Pickens played in all 17 games, hauling in 93 passes for 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns. His 65% success rate was the highest of his career and well above average.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This year has admittedly been more frustrating for the 25-year-old. Though he received healthy snap counts from the beginning of the season through Week 6, he was not putting up his 2025 volume in the statistics category.
 Recently, his snap share has actually decreased due to a lingering hamstring issue. On Friday, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on 105.3 the FAN that Pickens is "hopeful" to play in the next game but may continue to be limited.
 The receiver has yet to miss a game in his Cowboys tenure, so it is likely he will suit up for Sunday's Week 9 contest at the Indianapolis Colts. Even if he is not getting many targets, he draws defenders with his big-play ability.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement On the season overall, Pickens has accumulated 39 receptions for 533 yards and two touchdowns. He is averaging 66.6 yards per game, although that number is heavily propped up by a 130-yard performance in Week 5.
 That said, he does remain towards the top of quarterback Dak Prescott's target list. Through Week 8, his 21.1% target share ranks second on the team by a healthy margin. With 39 catches on 62 targets, he brings in about 63 percent of balls thrown his way.
 Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (3) Jerome Miron-Imagn Images
 Dallas as a team is having a similar season to last year. Though they run one of the league's top offenses, their bottom-dwelling defense is really holding them back. Owner Jerry Jones has said that he will be reluctant to make moves at the trade deadline.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pickens should be able to go this Sunday, but in what capacity will not be determined until after kickoff at 1 p.m. ET.
